subject: Load certification & SLA test collaboration with BrightWave
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@brightwave.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-19T16:02:00Z
Subject: Load certification plan for BrightWave - proposed windows & success criteria

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Attached is a focused "load certification" plan (bw_load_plan_v1.xlsx) that maps Redwood's test harness to the traffic profile you shared. High level summary:

- Goal: certify production readiness for the BrightWave inference pipeline and get signoff on the performance SLOs needed for go-live planning.
- Target SLOs (post-tuning): p50 latency < 120ms, p95 latency < 350ms, sustained throughput 250 requests/sec (across the cluster), tail spikes allowed up to 450 rps for short duration (<= 30s).
- Acceptance tests: steady-state 30m run at 250 rps; three scheduled spike windows; KV/prefix cache warm-up; functional correctness smoke after each run.
- Environments: we propose running in your staging cluster and then repeating one run in our preprod with identical config.

Can you confirm the following by EOD Tuesday?
1) Which 2-hour window on Wednesday/Thursday next week works best for a steady-state run from your side?
2) Any gating that would block us from running short spike tests against staging (e.g., maintenance windows, rate-limits)?
3) Do you want Redwood to own orchestration (we run the harness and post the dashboard) or do you prefer to run the harness and we consume the results?

I've CC'd Monica (on-the-ground test lead), Ben (service engineering), and Laura (CS owner) so we can assign roles once we have the window.

Attachments: bw_load_plan_v1.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out quickly.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Sarah Cho <sarah.cho@brightwave.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-engineer@brightwave.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Load certification plan for BrightWave - proposed windows & success criteria

Thanks Michael — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. Quick answers below and we've attached our traffic outline (brightwave_traffic_profile.json).

- Windows: Wednesday 2026-10-21 14:00-16:00 PT looks best for the steady-state run. We can also allow a 30m spike test at 15:00.
- Gating: staging has a soft cap at 1,000 concurrent connections for non-prod; we can temporarily raise to support your spike test but need 48h notice.
- Orchestration: BrightWave prefers Redwood to run the harness and post results to the shared Grafana dashboard; ops-engineer@brightwave.com will monitor.

Acceptance note: procurement will still need the final resource estimate for Dedicated capacity, but this certification will feed that ask.

I'll loop in our SOC contact if we need to exchange any additional monitoring access.

—Sarah Cho
Director, Platform Engineering | BrightWave Analytics
Sarah.cho@brightwave.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, michael.grant@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-21T14:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Load certification plan for BrightWave - test owners & runbook

All — per Sarah's reply, Wed 2026-10-21 14:00 PT is confirmed. Action items below (I'll own orchestration with Ben):

1) Ben: prepare test harness + load generator config (use brightwave_traffic_profile.json). Ensure KV cache prefill step runs 20m before the steady window.
2) Monica (myself): run steady-state 30m at 14:10-14:40 then trigger three spike windows at 15:00, 15:06, 15:12 (each 30s). Capture full traces and token-level latency histograms.
3) Laura: coordinate with Sarah for temporary staging cap raise and confirm monitoring access. Post-run, collect acceptance signoff from BrightWave PM.
4) Michael: stand by for quick troubleshooting on model config / quantization toggles; be prepared to flip fallback model if tail latency > 450ms.

Runbook highlights (short):
- Warmup: 20m prefix warming; validate cache hit-rate >= 85% before steady run.
- Steady: 30m at target qps; p95 target = 350ms.
- Spikes: three 30s bursts to 450 rps; verify graceful degradation and no OOMs.
- Post-run: upload artifacts to shared drive, tag in HubSpot deal, and schedule a 30m readout within 24h.

Attaching run checklist (inline in Drive).

—Monica
Monica Patel
Test Lead, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-23T20:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Load certification plan for BrightWave - results & next steps

Hi Sarah / team —

Thanks for the collaboration this week. We completed the runs per the plan and uploaded artifacts to the shared folder. Summary highlights below (full artifacts attached: redwood_sla_test_results_20261023.zip):

- Steady-state (30m at 250 rps): p50 = 88ms, p95 = 320ms; CPU and GPU utilization within expected ranges; cache hit-rate averaged 87%.
- Spike windows (three x 30s to 450 rps): graceful tail increases observed; max p99 observed at 1.2s for spikes but recovered to baseline within 45s. No OOMs or infra errors logged.
- Regression note: one quantization config produced a small increase in tail latency; we reverted to the baseline quantized model for the third run and confirmed p95 recovery.

Artifacts & next steps: 
- Artifacts uploaded: redwood_sla_test_results_20261023.zip (raw traces, token latencies, sample payloads).
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/ops/bw-load-test-20261023 (live panels + annotations).
- Ask: can BrightWave provide preliminary signoff on "Performance Certification" based on the SLOs in the original plan? If yes, we will produce the final resource estimate for Dedicated capacity and schedule a handover to Solutions Engineering for go-live planning.

If the BrightWave PM wants a readout, let's schedule a 30m walkthrough early next week — I can demo the trace obs and explain the quantization trade-offs we observed.

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround — special thanks to Monica and Ben for running the harness.

—Michael
